A B2B SaaS platform (Series D) — Technology & SaaS engagement delivered by a 12-person team over 9 months, US scope, commercial model: build-transfer.

items: Deploy frequency up but incidents ate roadmap; error budgets decorative.
LLM features shipped without cost telemetry or eval gates; margin diluting.
SOC 2 evidence manual; enterprise deals stalled on security reviews.

blocks.x: The platform program delivered golden paths with SLO discipline and DORA instrumentation; the AI feature factory wired evaluations, guardrails and cost telemetry into the release train; and compliance-as-code produced continuous SOC 2 evidence — security reviews passed in days.

Here is the working rhythm, stated so you can hold us to it: weeks 1–2 produce the signed baseline: current per tenant performance, method note, and a control owner who co-signs every later claim. from week 3 the working slice goes live at business unit scope: shadow first, then canary, then promoted cohorts — each promotion justified by the eval gate, not enthusiasm. What holds the build together is discipline at the boundaries: models, agents and rules move through versioned, evaluated releases in A B2B SaaS platform (Series D), and every exception path degrades to human review, never to silence.. The build earns trust the same way every gate does: signals cross boundaries only through typed contracts in Data, Analytics & Lakehouse delivery, so a regression is a cohort, never an estate.
